mina: quick heads-up — on the canary pool with awq-int8 we observed a consistent accuracy dip on our summarization eval (~3.7% ROUGE-L drop).
ashwin: hmm, when did this start? any correlated infra changes?
mina: started after the batching change that enabled continuous batching + prefix cache reuse (rolled 2 hrs ago). no infra scaling events.
julia: logs look like we’re reusing KV entries across different prefix lengths when batch merges happen. possible key aliasing? attaching a small trace.
mina: reproducible locally with a 8k context test. if we set batcher to strict-window it goes away.
simon: could be hash collision in the cache key generation when tokens are joined from different requests. I saw similar with last year's streaming merge.
ashwin: can you paste the cache-key snippet?
julia: sure — snippet:```python
def cache_key(model, session_id, prefix_tokens):
    return f"{model}:{session_id}:{hash(tuple(prefix_tokens)) & 0xffffffff}"```
ashwin: oh the 32-bit truncation is dangerous when we concatenate different request prefixes under continuous batching. collisions plausible.
mina: changing to 64-bit reduced the ROUGE delta in my local run to ~0.4%.
simon: also check the normalization of token lists — trailing EOS vs not can change tuple shape but collide under short hashes.
ops-bot: deploy-started: rollback to previous batching config requested by @mina.
mina: for the canary we disabled prefix-cache reuse for multi-request merges and will re-enable after we confirm hash fix + gating.
julia: plan: (1) replace 32-bit hash with 64-bit (2) add explicit length salt to key (3) add a unit test that randomizes prefix concat ordering to catch collisions.
ashwin: also add an eval job that runs 1000 randomized merges against the gold set; fail if delta > 0.7% ROUGE-L.
simon: on the runtime side, if we detect a collision probability > threshold we should fall back to per-request isolation (slower but safe).
mina: agreed. can someone own the PR for the hash + tests?
julia: I’ll do it. expect WIP in ~3 hours.
mina: thanks. after julia's PR lands we should re-run canary with both strict-window and continuous to confirm parity.
ashwin: i'll queue the eval and set alert if regression persists.
ops-bot: deploy-finished: rollback applied to canary pool.
mina: wild idea for follow-up: consider ephemeral per-batch salts derived from request-ids to avoid long-term key space reuse — but we need to reason about cache hit rates.
simon: yeah that changes hit dynamics. include a hit-rate sim before trying.
mina: okay. short term: hash fix + salt length tweak + merged eval gate. long term: sim + perf tradeoff analysis.
nashwin: noted. closing loop once julia's PR + eval results are in. :thumbsup:
